land.text: 'an area south of the foothills of the Himalayas and north of the Indo-Gangetic Plain' around the capital Kapilavastu (the Kapilavastu page offers Piprahwa in Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh, and Tilaurakot in Kapilvastu Municipality, Nepal, which lie within a few kilometres of each other); Kosala to the west and south, 'the Koliya across the Rohni River to the east'; the page gives no boundary, so a 35 km disc stands for the republic

sources.note: Two proposed sites, Piprahwa (Uttar Pradesh) and Tilaurakot (Nepal); no coordinates, no dates.

notes: Dates are bridging: the page gives only 'c. 7th century' and 'c. 5th century' (no year for either), so both events are confidence 1. The page says the republic had become 'a vassal state of the larger Kingdom of Kosala' by the Buddha's time without a date; the matching vassal_start belongs to the Kosala dossier (sa-01-b), which does not carry it, so the whole life is drawn as an independent state. The Kalama republic (the map caption on the Shakya page: 'Vidudabha's conquest of Kalama, Sakya and Koliya') has no page of its own opened here. The Koliyas are the koliya dossier of this batch. The Rohini feud with the Koliyas (no year) moved no land. Gazetteer: Kapilavastu is not a place; a coordinate disc stands in.
